screen: Ask Watar · watar.html — Sufra’s app (sufra.iqaa.app/watar). The default viewer is Hala (Owner); ?as=reem|salma|yusuf|hala works as it does on Today. It is a conversation with Watar. Every answer is computed in the browser from window.SUFRA and window.JOBS (no network, no model), and every action Watar proposes waits in the dashed grey pen until a person approves it. Built as tools/p_watar.py, assets/js/watar.js and assets/css/watar.css, with the class prefix aw- (build.css already owns .wt-*, verified).
decision:
The two proposals are merged. Proposal 1’s conversation is the structure.

Why the conversation wins:
• The user asked for exactly that: «شات مع وتر».
• These questions chain: ‘Who is late?’, then ‘why?’, then ‘remind him’. Each step needs the last answer in view.
• An approval belongs beside the evidence that justifies it.
• One column is the shape of the phone the team works from.

Proposal 2 is a briefing first: a standing ‘This morning’ memo with an ask bar, pins and a tray. That answers a different brief and repeats the Overview’s job, so its layout, pins and tray are dropped. Five of its ideas are kept, because each is better on evidence:
(1) A ‘Read as’ line on every answer. It is the honest way for a rules engine to show how it read the question.
(2) Watar’s authorship marker is the neutral Ask Watar arch icon (n600). Violet on this page then marks only what waits for a person: drafts, Approve and people (guideline 1, ‘Violet is a person’).
(3) On phones, Ask Watar sits in the top bar beside Search. The tab bar fits five 64 px tabs in 359 px, and Clients, built in parallel, takes the fifth (6 × 64 = 384 > 359).
(4) The composer’s concentric geometry: a 56 px field with radius 14 and a 6 px inset gives a 44 px button with radius 8. This keeps PRODUCT.md’s 44 px target rule.
(5) A scheduled per-order reminder (‘Remind Rami today at 18:00’) for an order whose quote has not gone yet.

Four things change from both proposals, each on evidence:
(a) No red on this page with today’s data. Nothing is late or failed at 09:41, and the Overview uses red only for late facts (.at.late). A projected late reminder is drawn in the dashed grey pen and said in words.
(b) The line change becomes a handoff that the Line screen really shows. ‘Draft it on the Line screen’ opens line.html?wait=approval:A%20day, where it appears as the draft of version 4 (about 10 lines in line.js). Edits on the Line screen are in-memory today, so this behaves exactly like an edit made there.
  – Both proposals’ conditional waits (‘two days or until a day before’, ‘until 18:00 when under 3 days’) cannot be held by the line model. Its waits are fixed lengths: line.js offers An hour, A day, Two days, Three days and A week.
  – Proposal 1’s approved state, ‘Added to the draft of version 4’, would have pointed to a Line screen that does not show it.
(c) One shared clock in jobs.js:
  – It is order.js’s working-hours spread, pinned to SUFRA.done.
  – The client’s arch reads as open while its station’s wait runs.
  – It is computed on Sufra’s wall clock read as UTC.
  – Checked in a script: today the order page puts Reem’s price check for Office lunch at Fri 30 Oct, 14:00 and shows ‘The client approves’ as done on Sat 31 Oct, 14:30. Today records the check at 08:52 today.
  – Measured: Africa/Cairo leaves summer time on 30 Oct 2026, and local Date arithmetic there gives Office lunch’s lead time as 5 d 0 h 15 min instead of 4 d 23 h 15 min.
(d) One demo record is added: Reem logged Board breakfast at 08:30 today. The order page already places that step at 08:30 today, while Today and the Overview do not list it.

Scope, for one engineer in one pass:
• 4 new files and 11 small shared edits.
• The engine is one pure function, ask(), with 19 intents in order, so every answer can be checked by its text.

Known limits:
• Free text without a model will miss some phrasings. Starters, follow-ups, ‘Read as’, clarify turns and an honest fallback limit the damage.
• Arabic questions are not parsed this round.
• Phone keyboard behaviour on iOS Safari is NOT VERIFIED.
• The Overview’s ‘Needs attention’ does not list at-risk orders yet. V.risk is ready for that next round.
• The Clients screen edits the same NAV lines in p_line.py.

layout_desktop:
At 1440 × 900 with the sidebar open, the sheet is 1184 px wide (1440 − 248 sidebar − 8 desk). That leaves 1120 px of content inside the 32 px ap-wrap.

Head (padding-block 32/24, the td-head pattern):
• Eyebrow ‘Sunday 1 November · 09:41’ (14/20, n700). The time is in Fragment Mono 13 px and moves on each minute from 09:41.
• h1 ‘Ask Watar’ (31/44, letter-spacing −0.015em).
• Sub, 16/24, n700, max 60ch.
• At the inline end, bottom-aligned with the h1: .btn.small ‘New conversation’, shown once a question exists.
• No mark and no illustration.

Body:
• .aw-body is an inline-size container.
• At 940 px or more it is a grid, ‘minmax(0, 820px) 300px’, with a 48 px gap and justify-content: start.
  – At 1440: thread 772 + 48 + rail 300 = 1120.
  – At 1280: content is 960, so 612 + 48 + 300.
  – With the sidebar folded at 1440, content is 1296; the thread stops at 820 and the rail stays beside it.

Thread:
• An <ol>. Exchanges are 48 px apart, and each after the first opens with a 1 px n100 hairline 24 px above its question.
• Every turn is a grid: a 32 px marker column, a 12 px gap, then the content.
• Question turn:
  – The asker’s initial in a 24 px lilac circle.
  – Meta ‘Hala · 09:42’: 13/20, the name 700 ink, the time Fragment Mono 12 n700.
  – The question as h2: 18/26, weight 600, max 64ch.
• Watar’s turn follows 16 px later:
  – Marker: the Ask Watar line icon, 20 px, n600.
  – Meta ‘Watar · 09:42 · Read as: …’.
  – Lead: 16/24 ink, max 64ch.
  – One evidence figure. It spans the whole turn width from the marker’s start (772 px), with a 1 px n200 border, radius 12, padding 8/12 and a white ground.
  – Notes: 14/20, n700.
  – Drafts: max 620 px, in the content column, 24 px apart.
  – Links, then ‘Ask next’: a 13 px n700 label, then 14/20 ink links separated by middots.
• Prose stops at about 600 px. Figures use the full width.

Composer:
• The last child of the thread column: position sticky, inset-block-end 0, z-index 4.
• White, with a 1 px n200 hairline on top and padding 12/16 (the su-bar pattern, no fade).
• Field:
  – min-height 56, radius 14, 1 px n300 border; n600 on hover.
  – Focus: a 2 px violet outline and an ink border.
  – The textarea is 16/24 with 16 px padding and grows from 1 to 4 lines (120 px, then it scrolls).
• An ink .btn ‘Ask’, 44 px, radius 8, inset 6 px at the field’s inline end.
• On a short thread the band simply sits under the last turn; sticky only engages when the thread is taller than the view.

Rail:
• 300 px, n50, radius 16, padding 24.
• position sticky 16 px from the top, max-height calc(100vh − 32px), with its own scroll.
• Contents in order:
  – h2 ‘Waiting for you’ (15/22, 700) with a mono count, then its rows.
  – h3 ‘Decided here’ (13/18, n700), then its rows.
  – A 1 px n200 hairline with 24 px either side.
  – ‘What Watar reads’, with Sufra’s signature at k 0.5 (228 px wide).

Foot: ‘Runs on Iqaa’ and ‘Prototype: ask as Hala · Reem · Salma · Yusuf.’

Under 940 px of content the page is one column. A 1024 px window, for example, gives 1024 − 248 − 8 − 64 = 704.
• ‘What Watar reads’ becomes a details disclosure at the top of .aw-body.
• ‘Waiting for you’ becomes the one-line strip inside the composer band.

sections.name: Frame and ways in
sections.content:
Sidebar (tools/p_line.py):
• NAV = ['Overview', 'Today', 'Line', 'Orders', 'Ask Watar'] and PAGES['Ask Watar'] = 'watar.html'.
• NEXT = ['Clients', 'Settings'].
• When Clients lands, NAV becomes [..., 'Orders', 'Clients', 'Ask Watar'] and NEXT becomes ['Settings'] (PRODUCT.md’s order).
• The item is icon('Ask Watar', 20), then ‘Ask Watar’, then <i class='ap-n me' data-n-watar>, inside <li class='ap-li-watar'>. Its count is the number of drafts that wait for the person signed in.

Phones (under 900 px):
• .ap-li-watar is hidden from the tab bar.
• A 44 × 44 link, <a class='ap-ask' href='watar.html' aria-label='Ask Watar' title='Ask Watar'>, sits right after Search in the top bar. It carries the same icon in ink and an 8 px violet dot, <i data-n-watar-dot hidden>, with sr text ‘2 drafts wait for you’.
• It is hidden at 900 px and wider.

Ctrl/Cmd K (app.js):
• SCREENS gains { t: 'Ask Watar', s: 'Ask about the work; Watar answers from the line', href: 'watar.html' }.
• When nothing matches, the ‘Nothing matches’ line becomes one option: the arch icon and ‘Ask Watar: “<typed words>”’, opening watar.html?q=<words>.

Order page (order.js), live orders only: a .link, ‘Ask Watar why it waits’, in the Now card, opening watar.html?q=Why%20is%20<title>%20waiting%3F.
sections.interactions:
• app.js reads sessionStorage 'iqaa-watar:<viewer key>' on every page (in try/catch) and shows the count when it is above 0.
• On this page, watar.js rewrites the same two elements after every approve, discard or send.
• A link with ?q= asks once on arrival. watar.js then removes q with history.replaceState (keeping as), so a reload never asks twice.

sections.name: Head
sections.content:
• Eyebrow: ‘Sunday 1 November · 09:41’ (.td-day; the time in Fragment Mono, data-now).
• h1: ‘Ask Watar’.
• Sub: ‘Watar answers from Sufra’s line and its orders. It drafts; you decide.’
• Inline end: .btn.small ‘New conversation’, hidden until the first question.
• Under the head, the shared one-line note (.ap-note, role=status) with Undo.
• No logo, mark or hero: the arch already appears in the nav icon and on every answer.
sections.interactions:
• The time moves on each minute (setInterval 60 s, as on Today).

New conversation:
• Discards pending drafts and keeps decided ones.
• Clears the questions and re-renders the opening turn at the current time.
• Shows ‘Conversation cleared. 1 draft discarded with it.’ with Undo for 8 s. Undo restores everything.
• Puts focus in the composer.

sections.name: Opening turn
sections.content:
One Watar turn, computed when the conversation starts, with no question above it.
• An sr-only h2: ‘Watar’s summary at 09:41’.
• Meta: ‘Watar · 09:41’.
• Lead: ‘Nothing on Sufra’s line is late at 09:41. Two orders are at risk: for Office lunch and Board breakfast, the line’s reminder to the client would come after the event.’
• Then ‘Ask about an order, a person or the day. For example:’ and four starter rows (role=group, aria-label ‘Questions to start with’):
  – Who is late today?
  – Why is Nakhla’s order stuck?
  – What is waiting for Reem?
  – What is due by tomorrow?
  These are generated from the data; see Computations.

Variants:
• With no risk, the lead reads ‘Nothing on Sufra’s line is late at 09:41, and every timed wait ends before its event.’
• A risk whose reminder was approved adds ‘Omar was reminded at 09:44.’
sections.interactions:
• A starter asks its exact words, which appear as the asker’s question.
• Starter rows are 44 px buttons, full width of the content column, with n100 hairlines between them. Text 15/22 ink, underlined on hover. No icons, no chips.
• The opening turn stays first in the thread.

sections.name: Exchange: the question
sections.content:
• Markup: <li><article aria-labelledby='aw-q-n'>.
• Marker: the asker’s initial in a 24 px lilac circle (12 px, weight 700).
• Meta: the name (13/20, 700, ink) · the time (Fragment Mono 12, n700).
• The question is the h2 (id aw-q-n; 18/26, weight 600, max 64ch). It is the escaped text exactly as asked, never rewritten.
• No bubble, no fill, no right alignment: the question is the title of what follows.
sections.interactions:
• Text is selectable.
• ArrowUp in an empty composer recalls the last question.
• scroll-margin-block-start is 16 px. After asking, the page scrolls this heading to the top of the view (smooth unless reduced motion), because answers are read top down.

sections.name: Exchange: Watar’s answer
sections.content:
• Marker: the Ask Watar line icon (path M3 17h3c1.2-7.5 10.8-7.5 12 0h3), 20 px, n600. It marks authorship and is never violet.
• Meta: ‘Watar · 09:42 · Read as: Lunch for Nakhla, SFR-26-0031’ (13/20, n700). On phones the read-as part wraps onto its own line.
• Then, in this order and nothing else:
  – The lead: one or two sentences, 16/24 ink, max 64ch, tabular figures.
  – At most one evidence figure.
  – Up to three notes (14/20, n700).
  – Up to two drafts.
  – Links: ‘Open the order’, ‘Open Reem’s Today’, ‘See them in Orders’.
  – ‘Ask next’: up to three follow-ups not yet asked in this conversation.
sections.interactions:
Reading:
• For one beat (600 ms) the marker ticks: .running applies the existing tick keyframes, step-end.
• The lead slot reads ‘Reading Sufra’s line…’ in n700, and the composer is disabled.

The answer:
• The parts enter in reading order, half a beat each, an eighth of a beat apart (Beats.enter).
• Reduced motion: no beat and no entering; the answer appears at once.
• One polite live region speaks ‘Watar: <lead>’, plus ‘1 draft waits for your approval.’ when the answer made drafts.
• Focus stays in the composer.
• Follow-ups ask their own words. Order names link to order.html?code=….

sections.name: Evidence: order rows and the time strip
sections.content:
Order rows:
• Overview’s .at row, lifted into jobs.js as V.dueRow(j). Date first (‘Tomorrow’ + 12:30 in mono), then the title, ‘client, organization · N people’, and ‘At <station>’ with who, with its glyph.
• Used by the late, due and clients answers. A list longer than six shows six and ‘See all n in Orders’.

In the late answer, each risk row is followed, aligned 88 px in with the title column, by a reason (14/20 ink) and a time strip:
• Office lunch: ‘The quote link went to Omar at 08:52. If he doesn’t answer, the line reminds him on Tue 3 Nov at 08:52, 20 hours after the lunch.’
• Board breakfast: ‘Its quote waits for Reem to check my draft, since 08:30. Even if it went now, the line would remind Rami on Tue 3 Nov at 09:41, an hour and 11 minutes after the breakfast.’

The time strip is an SVG the width of its column, 58 px high (72 px with a second label row). It shows:
• The n200 day line (1.5 px), with midnight ticks (n300, 6 px) labelled ‘Sun 1’, ‘Mon 2’, ‘Tue 3’ (mono 11, n600).
• The wait as a lifted pen:
  – no stroke for its length;
  – a flat n100 band (16 px, radius 4) marking the time the pen is up;
  – its dot at the middle: ink once the wait has begun, n500 if not.
• The step before the wait as a straight (k 0.6) ending where the wait starts: solid ink when done (Office lunch’s link at 08:52), dashed grey when only supposed (Board breakfast).
• The reminder as a dashed grey straight where the wait ends.
• The event as a 1.5 px ink rule labelled ‘Lunch · Mon 12:30’.
• Today’s dashed ‘Now 09:41’ rule.
• The label ‘Reminder · Tue 08:52’ (mono 11, n700).

Labels are placed left to right and clamped inside the strip. A label drops to a second row when it comes within 8 px of a label already in the first. A day label that would collide is left out.

Measured positions:
• At 343 px: Now 52, the link 48, Mon 12:30 at 174, Tue 08:52 at 266, the breakfast at 265 and its reminder at 270.
• At 772 px: about 10.5 px an hour.
sections.interactions:
• Rows link to their order.
• The strip has no interaction. It is role=img, named by the reason sentence.
• It is redrawn when its column changes width (ResizeObserver), like Today’s day line.
• Time runs in reading order: dir=ltr on the SVG for now, mirrored with the signatures when Arabic comes.

sections.name: Evidence: one order
sections.content:
Head: SFR-26-0031 (mono) · Lunch for Nakhla (a link) · Maha, Nakhla Co. · 40 people · due Thu 5 Nov, 13:00, in 4 days.

The job’s line:
• V.journey(j, c), the order page’s own drawing, max-width 620 px.
• Caption from order.js: ‘2 of 16 steps done; the rest waits ahead in grey’.
• When the figure is narrower than 560 px, the metro strip (J.strip, with the person’s stations ringed) and ‘At Quote · step 1 of 3’ replace it.

The current station’s steps as rows: glyph, name and who, with the status at the end.

Facts as a dl (dt n700, dd ink, 14/20):

• My draft: ‘Musakhan rolls, Maqluba with chicken, Three salads, Kunafa trays · delivered at 12:30, with plates and cutlery for 40 · total [TOTAL]’.

Variants:

sections.name: Evidence: people, stations, today and lead time
sections.content:
Person (‘What is waiting for Reem?’):
• Mini rows, .aw-mn: Today’s .mn rules copied into watar.css, because today.css and orders.css both define .dn and .dn-t.
• Each row: code, title and people; the metro strip with her stations ringed violet; the glyph and ‘At Quote: Watar drafts the quote · since 08:30 · due Tue 3 Nov, 08:30’.
• Order by due: Board breakfast, Lunch for Nakhla, Graduation dinner.
• Under the rows: ‘Done today: 08:30 logged Board breakfast · 08:52 checked the prices for Office lunch · 09:20 logged Engagement lunch.’ and ‘Next to reach her: Engagement lunch, at Quote.’

Team (‘Who is busiest?’): four rows, each with the initial, name, role and ‘3 waiting · 3 done today’ (counts in mono).

Stations (‘Where are the jobs?’):
• Eight rows in line order, with the branch indented under Client approval.
• Each row: the name, the count (mono 17) and what its orders wait on, e.g. ‘Reem’, ‘Rania; Omar in the two-day wait’, ‘sending Lina a receipt’.
• The station with the most is set in bold.

Station (‘What happens at Client approval?’):
• Its steps as glyph rows: arch ‘The client approves’ (the client, from their link); lifted pen ‘Wait two days’; straight ‘Remind the client’, with its message.
• Its routes: ‘Back to Quote when the client asks for a change’; ‘Over 30 people: on to Wholesale order, rejoining at Prepare; the rest go to Buy materials’.
• Who is there now.

Done today:
• One row per SUFRA.done entry, by time: the time in mono, the loop glyph, ‘Reem checked the prices · Office lunch SFR-26-0030’, then ‘Iqaa sent the quote link to Omar.’ in n700.
• Plus decisions made in this conversation, e.g. ‘09:44 Hala approved: Remind Omar now’.

Lead time:
• Three rows of title · came in · took, values in mono:
  – Workshop lunch: 7 d 2 h · 7 d 23 h
  – Birthday dinner: 7 d 4 h · 7 d 18 h
  – Clinic team lunch: 7 d 3 h · 7 d 7 h
• Then the note on the two short-notice orders.
sections.interactions:
• Every row links to its order, its person (today.html?as=…) or its station (orders.html?at=…).
• No inner scrollers: every part fits in 343 px.

sections.name: Draft from Watar: remind the client
sections.content:
Where it comes from:
• The late answer (Office lunch), the order answer of an at-risk order, or the remind intent.
• Keyed 'remind:<code>'. One per order; a new time replaces the pending one.

When it is allowed:
• The order is at Client approval with the arch open.
• Or, for a scheduled reminder, Client approval is still ahead.
• Otherwise the remind intent explains why there is none.

Default time:
• ‘now’ when the link has gone and the line’s reminder would land after the event.
• Sufra’s closing time today (18:00) when the link hasn’t gone yet.
• Otherwise the time that was typed.

Anatomy. No box: a 3 px dashed n500 rail runs down the inline-start edge (dash 4.5/4.5 = the grammar’s 1.4 × stroke), with 20 px of padding. Max 620 px.
• Head (13/20, n700): the violet arch glyph (20 px), ‘Draft from Watar · waits for you’.
• h3 (16/24, 700): ‘Remind Omar now’.
• What it does (15/22): ‘Runs Office lunch’s ‘Remind the client’ now, instead of on Tue 3 Nov at 08:52.’
• The action’s own strokes, dashed (a straight for now; a lifted pen then a straight for a later time), with ‘Omar gets this from Sufra:’.
• The message on n50, radius 8, padding 12/16, 14/20: V.fill(step.msg, j), i.e. ‘Hello Omar, a reminder about Office lunch: your quote is waiting at sufra.iqaa.app/q/0030.’
• What it won’t do (13/20, n700): ‘I won’t change the quote or the line.’
• Actions: Approve (.btn.primary), Discard (.link), ‘Change the time’ (.link).

Board breakfast’s version:
• h3 ‘Remind Rami today at 18:00’.
• ‘If the quote link has gone and Rami hasn’t answered by 18:00, Iqaa reminds him then, instead of two days after the link. For Board breakfast only.’
• ‘I won’t send the quote: Reem checks my draft first.’
sections.interactions:
Approve:
• In a quarter beat, Beats.set rewrites the arch as a violet loop (motion moment 3).
• A ‘now’ action’s straight is rewritten in solid ink. A scheduled action keeps its dashed strokes, because it is still ahead.
• The rail turns solid ink.
• The head reads ‘Approved by Hala · 09:44’.
• The body reads ‘Iqaa runs the reminder now. Office lunch still waits for Omar’s answer.’ For a scheduled reminder: ‘Iqaa reminds Rami today at 18:00 if he hasn’t answered by then.’, plus a ‘Take it back’ link until 18:00 on the demo clock.
• Focus moves to the status line (tabindex -1). The live region says ‘Approved: remind Omar now.’ The counts drop.

Discard: a quarter-beat fade, then a half-beat collapse to ‘Discarded: Remind Omar now · 09:45 · Undo’. Focus moves to Undo.

Change the time: fills the composer with ‘Remind Omar at ’ and focuses it.

In later answers the same key shows a one-line reference instead of a second copy, e.g. ‘Drafted above: Remind Omar now · waits for you · Show’, or its decided state.

sections.name: Draft from Watar: a change to the line
sections.content:
Offered when at least two risks come from the same timed wait. It appears in the late answer, after the note ‘Both come from one step of the line: Wait two days, at Client approval.’, and in the answer to ‘What happens at Client approval?’. Keyed 'line:approval-wait'.

The same pen-edge block:
• Head: ‘Draft from Watar · for the line’.
• h3: ‘Wait a day at Client approval, not two’.
• ‘In the draft of version 4, Client approval waits a day for the client’s answer before it reminds them.’
• The station drawn as three glyph rows. Only the changed step is in the dashed grey pen: violet arch ‘The client approves’; lifted pen, dashed, ‘Wait a day’ with ‘was two days’ in n700; ink straight ‘Remind the client’.
• Note: ‘Every new order’s client would be reminded a day sooner. Running orders keep version 3, so Office lunch still needs the reminder above.’
• Actions: ‘Draft it on the Line screen’ (an ink .btn, because it hands the work on; the decision is Publish, on the Line screen) and Discard.

‘Draft it on the Line screen’:
• Stores the state ‘sent’ at the current time, then navigates to line.html?wait=approval:A%20day.
• line.js applies the change to the draft line and shows ‘Draft of version 4 · not published yet’, with the note ‘Watar’s change is in the draft: Client approval waits a day instead of two. Publish it, or discard the draft.’

For anyone but the owner, the button is replaced by the text ‘The line is Hala’s to change.’

sections.name: Clarify, refuse and can’t-answer turns
sections.content:
Plain Watar turns: no evidence figure, no red, and always the nearest thing Watar can do.
• Ambiguous: ‘Four orders on the line are lunches. Which one?’ with choice rows ‘Office lunch · Mon 2 Nov’, ‘Lunch for Nakhla · Thu 5 Nov’, ‘Engagement lunch · Fri 13 Nov’, ‘Wedding lunch · Sat 14 Nov’, and the hint ‘Clinic team lunch and Workshop lunch are finished.’
• Remind whom: ‘Who should I remind? I draft reminders to clients whose quote is waiting: Omar, for Office lunch, or Rania, for Charity dinner.’ with two choices.
• Unknown order: ‘No order SFR-26-0040 is on Sufra’s line. The newest is SFR-26-0035, Engagement lunch.’
• Unknown person: ‘Ahmad isn’t on Sufra’s team in Iqaa. The team: Reem, Salma, Yusuf and Hala.’
• Not understood: ‘I couldn’t tie that to Sufra’s work. I answer about orders, people, stations and times on the line, for example:’ followed by the four starters.
• Money: ‘I can’t see money: Sufra has no prices in Iqaa yet, so every quote total is [TOTAL] until the price list is added. I can tell you which quotes are waiting, and for whom.’
• Outside the line: ‘I only read Sufra’s line: its orders, its people and its steps. I can’t see the weather, the road or what is in the kitchen.’
• Judging people: ‘I don’t rate people. Reem has 3 orders waiting; the oldest since Sat 31 Oct, 09:30.’
• A person called late: ‘Sufra’s line sets no time limit for a person’s step, so I don’t call a person late. Reem has 3 orders waiting; Board breakfast is due first.’
• Prediction: ‘I can’t know what Rami will do. If he hasn’t answered two days after the quote link goes, the line reminds him.’
• Won’t do:
  – ‘Checking the quote is Reem’s step, and approving it is Maha’s. I draft; I don’t approve for anyone.’ with ‘Open Reem’s Today’.
  – ‘The quote link goes to Maha by itself once Reem checks the prices. I don’t skip a person’s step.’
  – ‘I don’t cancel orders. Open the order to see where it stands.’
• Nothing to remind: ‘Lunch for Nakhla’s quote hasn’t gone to Maha yet: it waits for Reem to check it. There is nothing to remind her about.’
• A team member: ‘I draft reminders the line sends to clients. Reem sees what waits for her on her Today, Board breakfast first.’
• Client history: ‘In Iqaa, Nakhla Co. has one order with Sufra: Lunch for Nakhla, SFR-26-0031.’
• Help: ‘I answer from Sufra’s line: its orders, its people, its stations and the times on it. I don’t see prices, messages or stock, and nothing goes out until a person approves it. You can ask:’ followed by six example questions.
• Greeting: ‘Hello, Hala. Ask about an order, a person or the day.’ Thanks: ‘You’re welcome.’
sections.interactions:
• Choice and example rows ask their words.
• A choice sends only the order’s title. The pending intent from the clarify turn makes the next answer exact.
• Nothing in these turns creates a draft, except a remind choice.

sections.content:
• Sufra’s line signature: Beats.sig at k 0.5, 228 px, no names. It is a link to line.html with aria-label ‘Sufra’s line, version 3. Open the line.’, and carries the caption ‘Sufra’s line · version 3’.

sections.name: The engine: ask(text, ctx)
sections.content:
ask() in watar.js is a pure function.
• It reads S, J and V, plus ctx = { now (ms), viewer, drafts (state by key), pending (the intent of a clarify turn), asked (the questions so far, normalised) }.
• It returns { kind, read, lead, parts, notes, drafts, links, next, choices }.
• Renderers turn parts into HTML. ask() never touches the DOM, so the QA harness can check answers by their text.

1. Normalise: lower case; turn ’ and ‘ into '; drop 's; replace anything but a–z, 0–9, ':' and spaces with a space; collapse spaces.

2. Entities, built once from the data:
• Orders:
  – Tokens are the words of title, client and of, minus for, the, a, co, order and private.
  – A token is distinctive if exactly one order has it (computed), e.g. nakhla, board, breakfast, graduation, engagement, office, omar, darb, wedding, huda, family, meetup, charity, rania, book, clinic, birthday, workshop, maha, rami.
  – A shared token (lunch, dinner, haddad, studio) narrows but never resolves alone.
  – Codes: ‘sfr-26-0031’, ‘sfr 0031’, ‘0031’, or ‘order/#/no 31’ all mean SFR-26-0031.
• People: reem, salma, yusuf, hala. me, my, mine and i mean the viewer; owner means Hala.
• Stations, only when no order matched:
  – request
  – quote, quotes
  – client approval, approval
  – buy, buying, shopping, materials
  – wholesale, wholesaler
  – prepare, preparing, prep, kitchen
  – deliver, delivery, delivering
  – invoice, invoicing, billing
• Days: today; tomorrow; by tomorrow; this week (Sun 1 to Sat 7 Nov); weekday names (the next one, today included); ‘5 nov’ or ‘nov 5’.
• Times, for reminders: now; HH; HH:MM; am/pm; noon; ‘tomorrow at …’.

3. Resolution:
• Distinctive matches win.
• Two or more distinct orders lead to a clarify turn.
• With generic words only, live orders are the candidates.
• One live candidate resolves. No live candidate but one finished resolves to the finished order.

4. Intents, first match wins:
 a. Greeting or thanks (the whole text).
 b. Help: help, what can you, what do you know.
 c. Remind: remind, nudge, chase, follow up.
 d. Won’t do: approve, accept, confirm, sign, send, cancel, delete, skip, assign, pay.
 e. Money: total, totals, price of, prices of, cost, costs, revenue, profit, paid, money, how much, earn, income.
 f. Outside the line: weather, rain, traffic, road, roads, stock, fridge, supplier, news.
 g. Judge: slow, lazy, fast, good, bad, best, worst, rate, rating, performance, productive, blame — with a person.
 h. Predict: will, going to, likely, chance — with approve, answer, reply, pay or accept.
 i. Late: late, behind, overdue, delayed, on time, risk, at risk, in time, miss; also stuck, blocked or held up when no order is named.
   – With an order, it gives the order answer.
   – With a person, it gives ‘no time limit for a person’s step’.
 j. Lead time: how long, take, takes, took, average, usually, lead time.
 k. Client history: before, history, again, how many orders, regular — with a client or organization.
 l. Done: done, finished, did, completed. With ‘this week’ it lists finished orders; otherwise today’s steps, or one person’s.
 m. Order present: why, stuck, waiting, where, status, next, left, ahead, when, due, or the order alone. Gives the order answer.
 n. Person present, or team, busiest, everyone, who has the most. Gives the person answer, or the team answer.
 o. Clients: client, clients, customer, customers — with waiting, answer, answered, approve, pending or reply.
 p. Station present: that station’s answer.
 q. Stations: where are, bottleneck, which station, most orders, load, the line. Gives the load answer.
 r. Due: due, deadline, today, tomorrow, this week, a weekday or a date. Gives the due window.
 s. Otherwise:
   – an unknown capitalised name after for, is, did or has → not on the team;
   – a code with no order → no such order;
   – else not understood, with the four starters.

5. A clarify turn sets ctx.pending to its intent. A next question that is only an entity takes that intent.
sections.interactions:
• Typed questions, starters, follow-ups, choices and ?q= all go through ask().
• Answers read this conversation’s decisions. Asked again after an approval, Office lunch shows ‘Reminded at 09:44 · approved by Hala. The lunch still needs Omar’s answer.’ and stays listed as at risk.
• All user text is escaped (Beats.esc) before it is rendered.

sections.name: Conversation storage and lifecycle
sections.content:
• Per viewer, in sessionStorage 'iqaa-watar:<key>':
  { v: 1, startedAt, asked: [{ q, at, pending }], drafts: { '<key>': { state: 'pending'|'approved'|'discarded'|'sent'|'replaced', at, by, when } }, text }
• Every read and write is wrapped in try/catch.
• Nothing is written to sufra.js. The line handoff travels only in the URL.
sections.interactions:
On load:
• The thread is rebuilt by re-asking each stored question with its own stored time as now, so old answers read exactly as they did. The opening turn uses startedAt.
• The page scrolls to the last question.

If storage is blocked, every visit starts fresh and nothing else changes.

sections.name: Shared clock and the order page
sections.content:
jobs.js views(J, S) gains:
• T and fmt (Sufra’s wall clock, read as UTC).
• delivered and late (moved from overview.js).
• restHours.
• clock(j): order.js’s working-hours spread, with S.done pinning and the open client arch.
• journey(j, c) (moved from order.js).
• dueRow(j) (moved from overview.js’s att()).
• risk(j, now), fill(msg, j) and span(ms).

order.js then calls V.clock, V.journey and V.fmt.
• A step whose state is ‘open’ shows ‘Waiting for <client>’ (b) instead of a time, and keeps a solid glyph.
• The Now card gets the ‘Ask Watar why it waits’ link.

overview.js calls V.dueRow and V.delivered. Its output is identical, except what the new done record adds.
sections.interactions:
After the change, the order page agrees with Today and with Watar:
• SFR-26-0030: ‘Reem checks the prices’ at Sun 1 Nov, 08:52; ‘The client approves’ reads ‘Waiting for Omar’; since Sun 1 Nov, 08:52.
• SFR-26-0027: since 09:05.
• SFR-26-0035: ‘Reem logs the order’ at 09:20.
• SFR-26-0034: since 08:30.
• Unpinned orders keep today’s values: Nakhla, Sat 31 Oct, 09:30. The exception is Family dinner, whose Cairo-local value of 14:15 becomes 14:30 for every viewer.

identity_details:
Drafts are written in the dashed grey pen, the same pen as Build’s drafts and test runs.
• A 3 px n500 rail runs down the draft’s inline-start edge. The dash is 4.5/4.5, the grammar’s 1.4 × stroke.
• The action’s own strokes come from IQ.glyph(kind, {test: true}).
• The head carries the violet held arch, because it waits for a person; the system page’s ‘Draft from Watar’ does the same.
• Approving rewrites the arch as a violet loop in a quarter beat (motion moment 3) and writes a ‘now’ action’s straight in solid ink. The rail turns solid ink.
• A scheduled action keeps its dashed stroke under the solid rail, because it is still ahead.
• n500 is 3.95:1 on white and 3.62:1 on n50, above 3:1. Build’s n400 is 2.85:1.

The time strip draws the line’s timed wait as the grammar’s lifted pen at its real length.
• No stroke while the pen is up, a quiet n100 band for that time, and the dot at the middle.
• The step before it is ink when done and dashed when only supposed. The reminder after it is dashed, because it is ahead.
• The event is a solid ink rule; Now is Today’s dashed rule.
• The risk reads as a picture: the lunch falls under the lifted pen, and the reminder lands after it.

An order answer draws the order page’s own journey (V.journey, moved into jobs.js).
• ‘Stuck’ is where the pen stopped, and the drawing matches order.html stroke for stroke.
• The client’s open arch is drawn solid, because it is real and waiting.

Every who-or-where phrase starts with its step glyph, always with words beside it: an arch for waiting on a person or client, a loop for a person’s task, a straight for a step that runs by itself, a lifted pen for a timed wait.

Watar’s authorship marker is the Ask Watar line icon (the arch with its lead-in and lead-out), 20 px in n600.
• While Watar reads, it ticks on the beat (step-end, 600 ms), the running state Today and Build already use.
• No face, no avatar, no sparkle, no typing dots, no bubbles.
No red with today’s data. Red stays the grammar’s ‘failed or late’ and the Overview’s ‘late’ (.at.late). A projection is drawn in the dashed grey pen and said in words.
Fragment Mono sits in data positions: meta times, codes, counts, strip labels and lead-time cells. Sentences stay in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next with tabular figures, as Today’s due lines do.
The rail names Watar’s source with Sufra’s signature at k 0.5 (228 px), the one place on the screen where the line itself is the subject (guideline 5).

Answers are built from the product’s own parts: Overview’s .at rows, Today’s mini rows and metro strips, the order page’s journey and station rows. Watar’s answers read as Sufra’s screens, not as a chatbot’s.
computations:
Clock:
• now = T(S.dayIso + 'T' + S.now) plus the whole minutes since the page opened, at real speed (today.js’s minutes()).
• T(iso) = Date.parse(iso + 'Z'), formatted with getUTC*. Every demo time is Sufra’s wall clock, so neither the viewer’s timezone nor a late-October DST change can move it.
• Answers use the moment of asking. The opening turn uses startedAt.

Live, finished, delivered, late:
• live = !j.finished: 10 orders.
• finished: 3 orders.
• V.delivered(j): the index of j.at in J.main is greater than Deliver’s. Only Book launch reception, at Invoice.
• V.late(j) = V.days(j.iso) < 0 && !V.delivered(j). None at 09:41.
• These are overview.js’s rules, moved.

Step clock, V.clock(j) → { steps, nowAt, t[], open, since, state(i) }:
1. steps = J.route(j) flattened. nowAt = the index of (j.at, j.step), or steps.length when finished.
2. open = the steps before nowAt, in the job’s current station, that are held by ‘The client’. The arch stays open while its station’s wait and reminder run.
3. Pins: each S.done entry for j.code sets the step named d.step, and the next kinds.length − 1 steps that are before nowAt, to dayIso + d.time.
4. Every other done step that isn’t open is spread over working hours (S.hours) between the previous pin (or opened) and the next pin (or the end), rounded to the quarter hour. This is order.js’s at() unchanged.
5. The end is now for a live order and T(finished) for a finished one.
6. since = the time of the last timed step before nowAt.
Results (since): Nakhla Sat 31 Oct 09:30 · Board breakfast Sun 08:30 · Graduation dinner Sat 15:45 · Engagement lunch Sun 09:20 · Office lunch Sun 08:52 · Wedding lunch Sat 13:00 · Family dinner Sat 14:30 · Meetup coffee break Sun 09:05 · Charity dinner Sat 31 Oct 11:30 · Book launch reception Sat 12:15.

Risk, V.risk(j, now). Only for live orders that are not delivered and still have Client approval current or ahead:
• linkAt = clock.since when j.at is 'approval'; otherwise now (‘even if the quote went now’).
• remindAt = linkAt + restHours(wait.who) × 1 h. Two days = 48 h.
• At risk when remindAt > T(j.iso).
• Also at risk when the real timed waits ahead, outside the approval timeout, added to now end after the event. None today.
At 09:41 this gives exactly two orders:
• Office lunch: Tue 3 Nov 08:52, 20 h 22 min after Mon 2 Nov 12:30.
• Board breakfast: Tue 3 Nov 09:41, 1 h 11 min after 08:30.
Not at risk:
• Nakhla: Tue 09:41, 2 d 3 h before its lunch.
• Charity dinner: Mon 2 Nov 11:30.

Line-change suggestion. Made when at least two risks share one wait step:
• Take the longest option in line.js’s list (An hour 1, A day 24, Two days 48, Three days 72, A week 168 h) that is shorter than the current wait and ends every current risk’s reminder before its event.
• Office lunch with a day: 08:52 + 24 h = Mon 08:52 < Mon 12:30.
• Board breakfast with a day: 09:41 + 24 h = Mon 09:41 < Tue 08:30.
• Result: ‘A day’.

Due windows: V.days(j.iso) in the window, !delivered, sorted by iso.
• By tomorrow = days 0–1: Meetup coffee break (16:00 today), Office lunch (tomorrow 12:30) and Family dinner (tomorrow 20:00). That is the Overview’s 3.
• Book launch reception is named in a note, which explains why Orders says 4.
• This week = days 0–6 adds Board breakfast, Lunch for Nakhla and Graduation dinner.

Person:
• waiting = live orders whose step is theirs, sorted by iso.
• Position on Today = the index in that list + 1.
• done = their S.done entries.
• coming = Today’s coming() rule: the first step of theirs ahead, by distance, top 4.
Reem: 3 waiting (Board breakfast, Nakhla, Graduation dinner); 3 done (08:30, 08:52, 09:20); next to reach her: Engagement lunch, at Quote. Team counts are the same per person.

Stations: live orders per j.at, including the branch.
• Request 1, Quote 3, Client approval 2, Buy materials 0, Wholesale order 1, Prepare 1, Deliver 1, Invoice 1.
• The lead names the largest: ‘Quote holds the most: 3 of 10 orders, all waiting for Reem.’
• A station’s steps and routes come from line().

Lead time:
• took = T(finished) − T(opened): Workshop lunch 7 d 23 h · Birthday dinner 7 d 18 h · Clinic team lunch 7 d 7 h.
• came in = T(iso) − T(opened): 7 d 2 h · 7 d 4 h · 7 d 3 h.
• Live at-risk orders: Office lunch came in 4 d 23 h ahead, Board breakfast 2 d 14 h.
• Always followed by ‘Three orders are too few to call it a pattern.’

Order facts:
• steps done = nowAt of steps.length (2 of 16 for Nakhla).
• ahead = J.ahead(j).length (13).
• The branch applies when j.people > route.over (40 > 30).
• Waits ahead = the sum of restHours over ahead steps (48 + 24).
• Time left = T(j.iso) − now (4 d 3 h).
• The kitchen’s day-before reminder = T(j.iso) − 24 h (Office lunch: today at 12:30).

Reminder time:
• ‘now’ when the link has gone and remindAt is after the event.
• S.hours.close today (18:00) when the link hasn’t gone and now is before the close.
• A typed time is accepted only if it is later than now, earlier than remindAt and earlier than the event. Otherwise Watar says why.

Starters:
• Fixed: ‘Who is late today?’.
• ‘Why is <short name>’s order stuck?’ for the live order waiting longest at a team member’s step: Nakhla, since Sat 31 Oct 09:30. The short name is the first word of j.of, or the client for a private order.
• ‘What is waiting for <person with the most waiting>?’ gives Reem (3), or ‘me’ when that person is the viewer.
• Fixed: ‘What is due by tomorrow?’.

Ambiguity: ‘lunch’ matches 4 live orders (Office lunch, Lunch for Nakhla, Engagement lunch, Wedding lunch) and 2 finished ones (Clinic team lunch, Workshop lunch). ‘dinner’ matches 3 live and 1 finished. Choices are sorted by due.

Time strip geometry:
• t0 = today 00:00; t1 = the midnight after max(due, remindAt). Both strips today run Sun 1 to Wed 4 Nov (72 h).
• x(t) = 8 + (t − t0) / (t1 − t0) × (W − 16).
• At W 343: 4.54 px an hour, Now 52, Mon 12:30 at 174, Tue 08:52 at 266.
• At W 772: about 10.5 px an hour.
Rail counts: 10 on the line, 3 finished this week, 4 people, 4 steps done today (S.done.length). ‘As of’ follows the demo clock.

Pending count:
• The drafts in this viewer’s storage whose state is 'pending'.
• Shown in the rail, in the sidebar count (data-n-watar) and as the phone dot.
• ‘Sent’, ‘approved’, ‘discarded’ and ‘replaced’ drafts don’t count.
states:
First visit: the opening turn with four starters.
• The rail says ‘Nothing Watar drafted waits for you.’
• The composer sits right under the starters, so the page never shows an empty gap.
Reading: for one beat the marker ticks, the lead reads ‘Reading Sufra’s line…’ and Ask is disabled. Reduced motion skips the beat.
Answered: lead, one evidence figure, up to three notes, up to two drafts, links and ‘Ask next’.

Answered, nothing wrong, e.g. ‘Is Wedding lunch on time?’:
‘Yes. Wedding lunch waits for Hala to order from the wholesaler, since Sat 31 Oct, 13:00; then the line waits a day for the delivery, long before Sat 14 Nov, 13:00.’ No draft.
Clarify, which order: the ambiguity choices, with finished matches named in a hint.
Clarify, remind whom: choices for the clients whose quote is waiting (Omar, Rania).
Not found: an unknown order code, or a name that is not on the team.
Not understood: an honest sentence and the four starters. Nothing is guessed.
Out of scope: money, outside the line, judging people, prediction. Each says what Watar can’t see and offers the nearest question it can answer.
Won’t do: approve, send, cancel or skip. Each names whose step it is and links there.
Draft pending: dashed rail and dashed strokes, a violet arch, Approve, Discard and ‘Change the time’.
Draft approved, now: violet loop, solid rail, the action written in ink, ‘Approved by Hala · 09:44’.
Draft approved, scheduled: violet loop, solid rail, the dashed action still ahead, ‘Take it back’ until 18:00 on the demo clock. After that: ‘Iqaa reminded Rami at 18:00.’
Draft taken back: pending again.
Draft discarded: one n700 line with Undo.
Draft replaced: ‘Replaced by the draft below · 09:47 · Show’.
Draft already made: a later answer shows a one-line reference instead of a second copy.
Line draft sent: ‘Sent to the Line screen at 09:46 · publish or discard it there’ and ‘Open the line’.
Line draft for a non-owner: ‘The line is Hala’s to change.’ in place of the button.
Empty question: an inline error under the field, with focus kept in it.
Unsent text: kept per viewer through a visit to an order page and back.
Returning: the thread and its decisions come back from sessionStorage, re-asked at their own times, and the page scrolls to the last question.
New conversation: questions cleared, pending drafts discarded, decisions kept, a one-line Undo for 8 s.
Storage blocked: every visit starts fresh. Nothing else changes.
Script or data missing: the HTML keeps its first thread item, ‘Watar can’t read Sufra’s line right now. Reload the page.’, and the composer stays disabled.

Own organization from sign-up (sessionStorage iqaa-org, as on Today):
‘Watar reads <Org>’s orders once your team adds one. Until then, try your line with a test job.’ with an ‘Open the line’ button. The composer is disabled.
Narrow (under 940 px of content): ‘What Watar reads’ becomes a disclosure. Pending drafts show in the composer strip while none is on screen.
Reduced motion: no ticking, no entering, no smooth scroll; the arch-to-loop swap is instant. Every message stays.
Long thread: older exchanges stay where they are. Lists longer than six show six and ‘See all n in Orders’.

accessibility:
Heading outline:
• h1 Ask Watar.
• Each exchange is an <article> whose h2 is the question, so heading navigation jumps from exchange to exchange. The opening turn has an sr-only h2.
• Drafts are h3.
• The rail’s h2s come last in DOM order.
DOM order matches reading order: head, note, disclosure (narrow), thread, composer, rail. Nothing is reordered with CSS.

One polite live region speaks only Watar’s lead and the number of new drafts, e.g. ‘Watar: No one is late… 2 drafts wait for your approval.’ The thread itself is not a live region, so a whole answer is never read out unasked.

Accessible names carry their object, e.g. ‘Approve: remind Omar now’, ‘Discard: wait a day at Client approval’. Starters, follow-ups and choices sit in role=group with labels ‘Questions to start with’, ‘Ask next’ and ‘Which order?’.

Glyphs are aria-hidden, with words always beside them.
• Time strips are role=img, named by the reason sentence.
• The journey keeps order.js’s label.
• The rail signature link is named ‘Sufra’s line, version 3. Open the line.’
No state relies on colour alone: a dashed versus solid rail comes with ‘waits for you’ or ‘Approved by Hala’, and arch versus loop with the same words.

Frame fix: the sidebar’s violet counts sit on the n100 desk at 4.12:1 (12 px text). Both counts (Today’s and Ask Watar’s) become an n800 number with a 6 px violet dot before it, matching the folded sidebar’s dot. The phone badge (white on violet) stays.

Targets:
• Approve, Ask and every row button are at least 44 px.
• Inline text links appear only in prose and in desktop follow-ups (pointer: fine); under pointer: coarse those become 44 px rows.
• The top-bar Ask Watar button is 44 × 44.
Keyboard: Enter asks (not while composing, for IMEs), Shift+Enter adds a line, ‘/’ focuses the field, ArrowUp recalls, Esc clears. No traps; Ctrl/Cmd K still opens search.
Reduced motion: no ticking, entering or smooth scrolling, and the arch-to-loop swap is instant. Every message stays.
The field is 16 px so phones don’t zoom. The page reflows at 320 px with no sideways scroll and no inner scrollers.
lang='en' and logical properties throughout. The strips and the journey run in reading order (dir=ltr on the SVGs for now), to be mirrored with the signatures when Arabic comes.
